potential_business.body: Plausible hotel business tied to MIP CANCUN 2026 includes guestrooms and/or group room blocks for delegates, speakers, organizers and exhibitors; meetings or catering only when the programme still needs off-site or overflow space. Because a venue is already confirmed elsewhere, the realistic pathway is lodging overflow, faculty/housing packages, or relationship-building for a future edition — not claiming the contracted venue is available to rebook. why_this_hotel.title: Why this hotel
why_this_hotel.body: Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún offers an all-inclusive resort product, 507 rooms, a large ballroom and 12 breakout rooms near the airport.
advantages: this hotel is an oceanfront Cancún Hotel Zone all-inclusive resort with meetings capacity — aligned to incentive, congress-delegate, and resort-format programmes when organizers shortlist that product.
limitations: A venue is already confirmed elsewhere — treat the present edition as competitive capture / overflow / ancillary lodging unless a room block or housing RFP is separately evidenced as open.
All-inclusive resort format may be a mismatch for organizers seeking European-plan urban hotels or convention-center-adjacent inventory — confirm product preference before pitching.
Incumbent or published venue context: Moon Palace Cancún — use as competitive context, not as proof this hotel is selected.

Position Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive as a Chapultepec-corridor option for rooms and compact meetings when itineraries align — not as a confirmed preferred hotel. Most important qualification: Ask who coordinates lodging and meetings for visiting teams, and whether a preferred hotel or TMC already exists. Seek a named travel/meetings owner or a clear referral as the next commercial outcome. Act now while recent public activity is still a natural conversation opener.
qualificationQuestions: Who owns lodging and meeting decisions for HealthyHome, LLC visitors in Mexico City?
When teams or partners stay overnight near Chapultepec / Reforma / Polanco, do you already have preferred hotels or a travel-management process?

why_this_hotel.title: Why this hotel
why_this_hotel.body: Realistic option: Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive fits when Continental's relevant work brings people into the commercial core of Cancún (Cancún). Facility match: guestrooms and compact meetings/training are the plausible ask; do not invent travel times or exclusive advantages. What could prevent a win: itineraries locked to another corridor, an existing preferred hotel, or no overnight visitor pattern. Compelling when: visitors need a commercial address near this property and the account is still open to hotel introductions.
advantages: Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive sits in the commercial core of Cancún — a realistic base when Continental visitors meet near that corridor rather than only at a distant campus.

Corporate visitors who need guestrooms plus compact meeting space can be pitched on the hotel's location and facilities once itinerary geography is confirmed — not because the company and hotel merely share a city label.
When itineraries are not locked to a suburban campus, introducing Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive for rooms and small meetings is a defensible first conversation.
limitations: Competing properties closer to a verified office or client site can win on commute convenience; no preferred-hotel agreement or confirmed booking pattern is on file.
The hotel wins when visitor nights and meetings align with the commercial core of Cancún geography and when the account still lacks a locked preferred hotel — both conditions need qualification.

why_this_hotel.title: Why this hotel
why_this_hotel.body: Realistic option: Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive fits when LivePURE's relevant work brings people into the commercial core of Cancún (Cancún). Facility match: guestrooms and compact meetings/training are the plausible ask; do not invent travel times or exclusive advantages. What could prevent a win: itineraries locked to another corridor, an existing preferred hotel, or no overnight visitor pattern. Compelling when: visitors need a commercial address near this property and the account is still open to hotel introductions.
advantages: Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive sits in the commercial core of Cancún — a realistic base when LivePURE visitors meet near that corridor rather than only at a distant campus.

Corporate visitors who need guestrooms plus compact meeting space can be pitched on the hotel's location and facilities once itinerary geography is confirmed — not because the company and hotel merely share a city label.
When itineraries are not locked to a suburban campus, introducing Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive for rooms and small meetings is a defensible first conversation.
limitations: Competing properties closer to a verified office or client site can win on commute convenience; no preferred-hotel agreement or confirmed booking pattern is on file.
The hotel wins when visitor nights and meetings align with the commercial core of Cancún geography and when the account still lacks a locked preferred hotel — both conditions need qualification.

why_this_hotel.title: Why this hotel
why_this_hotel.body: Realistic option: Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive fits when Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste (ASUR)'s relevant work brings people into the commercial core of Cancún (Cancún). Facility match: guestrooms and compact meetings/training are the plausible ask; do not invent travel times or exclusive advantages. What could prevent a win: itineraries locked to another corridor, an existing preferred hotel, or no overnight visitor pattern. Compelling when: visitors need a commercial address near this property and the account is still open to hotel introductions.
advantages: Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive sits in the commercial core of Cancún — a realistic base when Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste (ASUR) visitors meet near that corridor rather than only at a distant campus.

Corporate visitors who need guestrooms plus compact meeting space can be pitched on the hotel's location and facilities once itinerary geography is confirmed — not because the company and hotel merely share a city label.
When itineraries are not locked to a suburban campus, introducing Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive for rooms and small meetings is a defensible first conversation.
limitations: Competing properties closer to a verified office or client site can win on commute convenience; no preferred-hotel agreement or confirmed booking pattern is on file.
The hotel wins when visitor nights and meetings align with the commercial core of Cancún geography and when the account still lacks a locked preferred hotel — both conditions need qualification.

opportunities.hotelOpportunityThesis: Conditional meetings-and-training fit, not an incentive-resort lead. The interstate audience supports plausible out-of-market accommodation, while the two-day programme supports meeting space, working meals and hybrid AV. Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive is a candidate for future sourcing, not the verified historical venue: its official Gran Condesa page offers divisible meeting space and videoconferencing capability. For a group around the historical scale, request an appropriately sized partition rather than the full ballroom. The Hotel Zone all-inclusive setting is only commercially credible if the buyer accepts the location, total cost, public-service purpose and an itemized business package; do not lead with beach leisure or incentives.
opportunities.guestroomDemandStatus: Plausible but unqualified. Interstate participation creates a credible travel signal, not evidence of hotel stays, a central room block or overnight entitlement. Approximately 80 participants is not a guestroom count; hybrid participation further prevents converting attendance into lodging demand. No booked property, room nights, arrival/departure pattern, payer, rooming list or lodging contract was verified. Do not forecast guestrooms from this historical edition.

revenue.note: At least one credible hotel revenue mechanism is required — guestrooms are optional.

facts: Official state reporting identifies the fourth encounter, Cancún destination, approximately 80 participants and two working days beginning with the 18 August 2026 inauguration.
The municipality explicitly describes this edition as hybrid; at least one senior federal participant joined virtually.
The audience included state victim-attention commissions, federal/state authorities, specialists, the consultative assembly and civil society; it was professional training and coordination.

The 21 August official conclusion report records an agreement to promote a Mesa Nacional Permanente para el Fortalecimiento de la Atención a Víctimas; it does not announce a funded future hotel event.

The hotel’s official Gran Condesa page describes a room divisible into three spaces, videoconferencing capability and a published full-room classroom capacity of 720; a suitable partition and actual layout require confirmation.

The older official directory lists named administration and training contacts, while 2026 event reporting identifies a different commissioner from that directory; the directory is not reliable proof of current staffing.
uncertainties: The exact physical venue and any historical hotel, catering, AV, transport or lodging supplier remain unverified.

The official opening source confirms 18 August and two days, but does not explicitly state the closing date; 19 August is explicitly reported by a secondary source. The 21 August closing article is a publication date, not proof of a third or fourth meeting day.
The state release says 19 states but separately names host Quintana Roo after listing 19 others; do not turn that wording into a firm 19- or 20-delegation rooming calculation.
No public evidence located establishes a future edition, repeat Cancún destination, live venue search, room block, room nights, budget or authorized hotel signatory.

Current tenure of the older directory’s administration/training contacts is unverified; the directorio-beta still names Landy Beatriz Blanco Lizama as titular whereas August 2026 event reports name María Elena García Flores.
Actual participant accessibility needs, resort acceptance, approved travel/meal limits, hotel availability and commercial terms remain unknown.

commercialIntelligenceBrief.recommendedNextStep: Classify as historical programme / future procurement nurture. Send a short Spanish-language capability enquiry to CEAVEQROO’s published administration mailbox, first confirming its current officer and asking for the training/logistics owner. Reference the August encounter and ask whether a future meeting or follow-up to the proposed Mesa Nacional Permanente has an approved location, date and sourcing timetable; its proposed creation does not itself establish a hotel requirement. Only if Cancún demand is confirmed, seek permission to provide a nonbinding, itemized government-meeting proposal with an appropriately sized room, hybrid AV, working meals and optional guestrooms/transfers. Request written confirmation of buyer, budget authorization, supplier-registration requirements and the formal quotation/tender channel. Obtain competing venue requirements rather than assuming this resort or any historical incumbent. Exclude leisure/alcohol extras from the base business proposal, avoid gifts or preferential hospitality, and make no booking or award claims.

why_act_now.title: Why act now
why_act_now.body: Public-sector programme history may support relationship development for future editions, but no verified open procurement window or forthcoming bookable edition has been confirmed from public research alone.

facts_and_uncertainties.title: Established facts and uncertainties
facts: Official state reporting identifies the fourth encounter, Cancún destination, approximately 80 participants and two working days beginning with the 18 August 2026 inauguration.
The municipality explicitly describes this edition as hybrid; at least one senior federal participant joined virtually.
The audience included state victim-attention commissions, federal/state authorities, specialists, the consultative assembly and civil society; it was professional training and coordination.

The 21 August official conclusion report records an agreement to promote a Mesa Nacional Permanente para el Fortalecimiento de la Atención a Víctimas; it does not announce a funded future hotel event.

The hotel’s official Gran Condesa page describes a room divisible into three spaces, videoconferencing capability and a published full-room classroom capacity of 720; a suitable partition and actual layout require confirmation.

The older official directory lists named administration and training contacts, while 2026 event reporting identifies a different commissioner from that directory; the directory is not reliable proof of current staffing.
uncertainties: The exact physical venue and any historical hotel, catering, AV, transport or lodging supplier remain unverified.

The official opening source confirms 18 August and two days, but does not explicitly state the closing date; 19 August is explicitly reported by a secondary source. The 21 August closing article is a publication date, not proof of a third or fourth meeting day.
The state release says 19 states but separately names host Quintana Roo after listing 19 others; do not turn that wording into a firm 19- or 20-delegation rooming calculation.
No public evidence located establishes a future edition, repeat Cancún destination, live venue search, room block, room nights, budget or authorized hotel signatory.

Current tenure of the older directory’s administration/training contacts is unverified; the directorio-beta still names Landy Beatriz Blanco Lizama as titular whereas August 2026 event reports name María Elena García Flores.
Actual participant accessibility needs, resort acceptance, approved travel/meal limits, hotel availability and commercial terms remain unknown.

qualificationQuestions: Is a subsequent edition or Mesa Nacional Permanente session actually approved, and will it be in Cancún? What are the exact dates and delivery format?
Who owns programme logistics, who issues the purchase order or contract, and which entity pays meeting costs versus delegates’ travel?
How many people will attend physically each day, and which require funded guestrooms, on what arrival/departure dates and occupancy basis?
Was the August venue governmental, donated or commercially contracted, and is a future venue already reserved or subject to an existing agreement?
What room layouts, breakouts, private spaces, hybrid AV, internet performance, catering and accessibility accommodations are required?
Is a Hotel Zone all-inclusive resort permissible and competitive under the applicable travel limits, meal rules and value-for-money evaluation?
Which procurement procedure, supplier registration, submission channel, evaluation criteria, invoice documents, payment terms and cancellation conditions apply?

what_is_happening.title: What is happening
what_is_happening.body: National two-day in-person training and coordination meeting in Cancún for representatives of 19 states, federal and state authorities, specialists, civil society and the consultative assembly; the multi-state audience is a credible source of meeting, catering and some out-of-market lodging demand, but no hotel procurement or room block is stated.

potential_business.title: Potential business for this hotel
potential_business.body: Conditional meetings-and-training fit, not an incentive-resort lead. The interstate audience supports plausible out-of-market accommodation, while the two-day programme supports meeting space, working meals and hybrid AV. Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive is a candidate for future sourcing, not the verified historical venue: its official Gran Condesa page offers divisible meeting space and videoconferencing capability. For a group around the historical scale, request an appropriately sized partition rather than the full ballroom. The Hotel Zone all-inclusive setting is only commercially credible if the buyer accepts the location, total cost, public-service purpose and an itemized business package; do not lead with beach leisure or incentives.

advantages: Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive is commercially positioned against the evidenced activity geography — evaluate as an alternative or overflow venue, not a confirmed booking.
limitations: No verified hotel booking, RFP, or preferred-supplier agreement is established from public research alone.

why_act_now.title: Why act now
why_act_now.body: Public-sector programme history may support relationship development for future editions, but no verified open procurement window or forthcoming bookable edition has been confirmed from public research alone.

facts_and_uncertainties.title: Established facts and uncertainties
facts: Official state reporting identifies the fourth encounter, Cancún destination, approximately 80 participants and two working days beginning with the 18 August 2026 inauguration.
The municipality explicitly describes this edition as hybrid; at least one senior federal participant joined virtually.
The audience included state victim-attention commissions, federal/state authorities, specialists, the consultative assembly and civil society; it was professional training and coordination.

The 21 August official conclusion report records an agreement to promote a Mesa Nacional Permanente para el Fortalecimiento de la Atención a Víctimas; it does not announce a funded future hotel event.

The hotel’s official Gran Condesa page describes a room divisible into three spaces, videoconferencing capability and a published full-room classroom capacity of 720; a suitable partition and actual layout require confirmation.

The older official directory lists named administration and training contacts, while 2026 event reporting identifies a different commissioner from that directory; the directory is not reliable proof of current staffing.
uncertainties: The exact physical venue and any historical hotel, catering, AV, transport or lodging supplier remain unverified.

The official opening source confirms 18 August and two days, but does not explicitly state the closing date; 19 August is explicitly reported by a secondary source. The 21 August closing article is a publication date, not proof of a third or fourth meeting day.
The state release says 19 states but separately names host Quintana Roo after listing 19 others; do not turn that wording into a firm 19- or 20-delegation rooming calculation.
No public evidence located establishes a future edition, repeat Cancún destination, live venue search, room block, room nights, budget or authorized hotel signatory.

Current tenure of the older directory’s administration/training contacts is unverified; the directorio-beta still names Landy Beatriz Blanco Lizama as titular whereas August 2026 event reports name María Elena García Flores.
Actual participant accessibility needs, resort acceptance, approved travel/meal limits, hotel availability and commercial terms remain unknown.

recommended_next_step.title: Recommended next step
recommended_next_step.body: Classify as historical programme / future procurement nurture. Send a short Spanish-language capability enquiry to CEAVEQROO’s published administration mailbox, first confirming its current officer and asking for the training/logistics owner. Reference the August encounter and ask whether a future meeting or follow-up to the proposed Mesa Nacional Permanente has an approved location, date and sourcing timetable; its proposed creation does not itself establish a hotel requirement. Only if Cancún demand is confirmed, seek permission to provide a nonbinding, itemized government-meeting proposal with an appropriately sized room, hybrid AV, working meals and optional guestrooms/transfers. Request written confirmation of buyer, budget authorization, supplier-registration requirements and the formal quotation/tender channel. Obtain competing venue requirements rather than assuming this resort or any historical incumbent. Exclude leisure/alcohol extras from the base business proposal, avoid gifts or preferential hospitality, and make no booking or award claims.
qualificationQuestions: Is a subsequent edition or Mesa Nacional Permanente session actually approved, and will it be in Cancún? What are the exact dates and delivery format?
Who owns programme logistics, who issues the purchase order or contract, and which entity pays meeting costs versus delegates’ travel?
How many people will attend physically each day, and which require funded guestrooms, on what arrival/departure dates and occupancy basis?
Was the August venue governmental, donated or commercially contracted, and is a future venue already reserved or subject to an existing agreement?
What room layouts, breakouts, private spaces, hybrid AV, internet performance, catering and accessibility accommodations are required?
Is a Hotel Zone all-inclusive resort permissible and competitive under the applicable travel limits, meal rules and value-for-money evaluation?
Which procurement procedure, supplier registration, submission channel, evaluation criteria, invoice documents, payment terms and cancellation conditions apply?

opportunities.guestroomDemandStatus: UNCONFIRMED. International participation establishes a credible reason to ask about overnight stays, not evidence of a hotel allocation. Published attendance measures differ: opening reporting cites more than 300; WRI later reports more than 600; the government closing report cites more than 900, comprising more than 700 registered participants and more than 200 students. Do not convert any of these measures into guestroom demand.

revenue.note: At least one credible hotel revenue mechanism is required — guestrooms are optional.

opportunities.whyThisHotel: Qualified relationship-development prospect, not confirmed business on the books. The international public-sector programme supports plausible delegate lodging, hosted meals, technical breakouts and delegation services, but attendance is not a room-block commitment. Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive is a relevant Hotel Zone resort-meetings option rather than an assumed city-centre transient hotel. Its official meetings page advertises more than 2,000 square metres across 12 rooms; Gran Condesa publishes maxima of 1,200 theatre, 900 banquet and 720 classroom. These support consideration for a future competitively sourced forum or smaller associated meetings, subject to simultaneous-room layouts and production needs. For a Cancún Center programme, the more immediate positioning would be delegate/overflow lodging and separately approved functions, with transport between the hotel at Km 16.5 and venue at Km 9. No evidence connects this hotel to the 2026 event. Neither resort leisure demand nor a funded banquet should be assumed.
whyThisHotelAdvantages: Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive is commercially positioned against the evidenced activity geography — evaluate as an alternative or overflow venue, not a confirmed booking.
whyThisHotelLimitations: No verified hotel booking, RFP, or preferred-supplier agreement is established from public research alone.

The programme included keynote conferences, technical panels and working sessions; the closing report identifies four keynote conferences and five strategic thematic axes.
AMAM organized, IMOVEQROO served as local governmental host, and WRI México provided technical accompaniment.
The programme brought international authorities, development banks, multilateral organizations, industry and academia together; attendee totals are not lodging totals.
The selected hotel publicly markets convention facilities, lodging packages and 12 meeting rooms; it is not limited to small resort gatherings.
AMAM’s closing report identifies Campeche’s 35th ENAM as a follow-on national meeting, not a confirmed repeat Latin American forum in Cancún.
uncertainties: No verified future edition, recurrence commitment or Cancún venue-sourcing window.
No verified hotel partner, historical room pickup, future room block, budget, contract or room-night total.
Attendance reports use different totals/scopes; their reconciliation is not established.
No named dedicated forum hotel buyer or event-specific procurement/signing authority; directory appointments should be reconfirmed.
No verified tender reference or contracting method for this forum’s lodging, catering or venue services.
No verified banquet requirement, transfer schedule, hotel availability or complete event-accessibility audit.

what_is_happening.title: What is happening
what_is_happening.body: Cancún-hosted regional public-sector forum bringing together more than 300 authorities, specialists, multilateral organizations and sector representatives for conferences, panels, workshops and case analysis; this supports substantial meeting, banquet and delegate-service demand aligned with Cancún’s regional-airport and resort-meetings profile.

potential_business.title: Potential business for this hotel
potential_business.body: Qualified relationship-development prospect, not confirmed business on the books. The international public-sector programme supports plausible delegate lodging, hosted meals, technical breakouts and delegation services, but attendance is not a room-block commitment. Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive is a relevant Hotel Zone resort-meetings option rather than an assumed city-centre transient hotel. Its official meetings page advertises more than 2,000 square metres across 12 rooms; Gran Condesa publishes maxima of 1,200 theatre, 900 banquet and 720 classroom. These support consideration for a future competitively sourced forum or smaller associated meetings, subject to simultaneous-room layouts and production needs. For a Cancún Center programme, the more immediate positioning would be delegate/overflow lodging and separately approved functions, with transport between the hotel at Km 16.5 and venue at Km 9. No evidence connects this hotel to the 2026 event. Neither resort leisure demand nor a funded banquet should be assumed.

why_this_hotel.title: Why this hotel
advantages: Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive is commercially positioned against the evidenced activity geography — evaluate as an alternative or overflow venue, not a confirmed booking.
limitations: No verified hotel booking, RFP, or preferred-supplier agreement is established from public research alone.

why_act_now.title: Why act now
why_act_now.body: Public-sector programme history may support relationship development for future editions, but no verified open procurement window or forthcoming bookable edition has been confirmed from public research alone.

facts_and_uncertainties.title: Established facts and uncertainties
facts: The event website fixes the 2026 dates and Cancún Center venue; government reporting confirms the forum took place and concluded.
The programme included keynote conferences, technical panels and working sessions; the closing report identifies four keynote conferences and five strategic thematic axes.
AMAM organized, IMOVEQROO served as local governmental host, and WRI México provided technical accompaniment.
The programme brought international authorities, development banks, multilateral organizations, industry and academia together; attendee totals are not lodging totals.
The selected hotel publicly markets convention facilities, lodging packages and 12 meeting rooms; it is not limited to small resort gatherings.
AMAM’s closing report identifies Campeche’s 35th ENAM as a follow-on national meeting, not a confirmed repeat Latin American forum in Cancún.
uncertainties: No verified future edition, recurrence commitment or Cancún venue-sourcing window.
No verified hotel partner, historical room pickup, future room block, budget, contract or room-night total.
Attendance reports use different totals/scopes; their reconciliation is not established.
No named dedicated forum hotel buyer or event-specific procurement/signing authority; directory appointments should be reconfirmed.
No verified tender reference or contracting method for this forum’s lodging, catering or venue services.
No verified banquet requirement, transfer schedule, hotel availability or complete event-accessibility audit.

primaryContact.name: Angélica Vesga
primaryContact.company: Instituto de Movilidad del Estado de Quintana Roo
primaryContact.whyRelevant: Best first programme-routing contact: AMAM publicly assigns its technical secretariat to WRI México. Ask who owns future forum planning and hotel sourcing; no contracting authority established. Public route: angelica.vesga@wri.org.

secondaryContact.name: Sandra Baltazar
secondaryContact.company: Instituto de Movilidad del Estado de Quintana Roo
secondaryContact.whyRelevant: Operational alternative for programme and logistics routing. Public route: sandra.baltazar@wri.org. No hotel-purchasing authority verified.

recommended_next_step.title: Recommended next step
recommended_next_step.body: Treat this as a nurture/qualification lead. Send Angélica Vesga or Sandra Baltazar a short, non-binding capability introduction identifying the completed February forum and asking whether a future Cancún edition, training programme or delegation meeting is planned. Request the operational producer, sourcing timetable, payer and procurement lead before quoting. If IMOVEQROO will pay, route procedural questions to Recursos Materiales and confirm Aldo Koh’s current remit. Offer transparent lodging-only/overflow and meeting-plus-lodging options, without gifts, personal inducements or any implication that an unsolicited quotation creates an award. Internally, use the hotel’s official meetings enquiry route or the published hugo.aguilera@posadas.com address to obtain current specifications and date-specific availability. Do not seek retrospective 2026 bookings or assume the existing Cancún Center venue can be displaced.
qualificationQuestions: Is another Latin American forum or related training/delegation programme approved, and what are its exact destination and dates?
Who is the operational organizer, legal contracting entity, budget holder and authorized signatory for each service?
Is the main venue already committed, and is the requirement for overflow accommodation, a host hotel, ancillary functions or a new venue competition?
How many overnight delegates are actually funded, by whom, with what arrival/departure dates, occupancy mix and accessible-room needs?
What simultaneous plenary/breakout layouts, exhibition space, AV, Wi-Fi, interpretation and security are required?
Which meals are officially authorized, what may be included in an all-inclusive rate, and must alcohol or leisure extras be excluded or separately billed?
Which procurement regime, supplier registration, solicitation reference, submission deadline, evaluation criteria and payment conditions apply?
What accessible transfer, venue-route, stage, restroom and emergency requirements must be demonstrated?

opportunities.hotelOpportunityThesis: Strong product fit, but not a live 2026 lead for Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive. The published congress packages combine accommodation and meals, matching a residential all-inclusive resort rather than city-center transient demand. The hotel officially markets conference facilities, 12 meeting rooms, approximately 2,000 square meters of event space, catering and lodging packages. However, Grand Oasis was already the named 2026 venue; no Fiesta Americana booking or open venue search is established. Pursue the announced 2027 edition only after confirming whether venue sourcing remains open. Plenary/panel space is supported by the programme format; breakout rooms, private banquets, AV and transfers remain qualification items, not confirmed orders.
opportunities.guestroomDemandStatus: EXPLICIT HISTORICAL PACKAGE INCLUSION; NO CONFIRMED PROPERTY ROOM BLOCK. Option A advertised one person in one room at MXN 31,900; Option B advertised two people in one double room at MXN 41,900. Both included congress admission, three nights/four days of lodging for 24–27 March and meals. These are total participation-package prices, not hotel room rates or available hotel budgets. No 2026 attendance, room-block quantity, actual pickup or total room nights is verified. Accommodation terms and volume for 2027 are not yet established.

revenue.note: At least one credible hotel revenue mechanism is required — guestrooms are optional.

facts: The official event page and January 2026 dossier publish 24–27 March 2026 in Cancún; the event page names Hotel Grand Oasis.
The official page names all three candidate organizers and describes municipal policy panels and conferences.
Both advertised participation options expressly include three nights/four days of lodging and meals.
El Tambo issued a municipal travel authorization on 9 March 2026 specifically naming this congress and its dates.
The organizer’s upcoming-events page announces Congreso Internacional Regidores y Concejales 2027 in Cancún for March 2027, with further information forthcoming.
The organizer publishes named finance and executive leadership contacts, but does not identify an event hotel-procurement officer in the reviewed material.
uncertainties: Published dates, packages and travel authorization do not independently establish that the 2026 event took place as planned or establish actual attendance and room pickup.
No confirmed Fiesta Americana business, overflow requirement, current RFP, venue-change decision or 2027 venue commitment was found.
Exact 2027 dates, attendance, accommodation packages, room block, meeting layout and banquet requirements remain unverified.
Hotel contracting authority, payer allocation, procurement rules, approved budget and commercial terms require direct qualification.
Dossier figures such as more than 1,000 public servants refer to the series since 2019, not a verified 2026 delegate count.
No room-night or revenue forecast is justified by the available evidence.

facts_and_uncertainties.title: Established facts and uncertainties
facts: The official event page and January 2026 dossier publish 24–27 March 2026 in Cancún; the event page names Hotel Grand Oasis.
The official page names all three candidate organizers and describes municipal policy panels and conferences.
Both advertised participation options expressly include three nights/four days of lodging and meals.
El Tambo issued a municipal travel authorization on 9 March 2026 specifically naming this congress and its dates.
The organizer’s upcoming-events page announces Congreso Internacional Regidores y Concejales 2027 in Cancún for March 2027, with further information forthcoming.
The organizer publishes named finance and executive leadership contacts, but does not identify an event hotel-procurement officer in the reviewed material.
uncertainties: Published dates, packages and travel authorization do not independently establish that the 2026 event took place as planned or establish actual attendance and room pickup.
No confirmed Fiesta Americana business, overflow requirement, current RFP, venue-change decision or 2027 venue commitment was found.
Exact 2027 dates, attendance, accommodation packages, room block, meeting layout and banquet requirements remain unverified.
Hotel contracting authority, payer allocation, procurement rules, approved budget and commercial terms require direct qualification.
Dossier figures such as more than 1,000 public servants refer to the series since 2019, not a verified 2026 delegate count.
No room-night or revenue forecast is justified by the available evidence.

primaryContact.whyRelevant: Best documented financial entry point: the official team lists her role, and the congress payment instructions direct card-payment requests to leticia@img.org.mx. Ask her to identify the hotel contracting and programme logistics owner; her authority to select or sign for a venue is not established.

secondaryContact.name: Andrés Franco
secondaryContact.whyRelevant: Senior organizer-side routing contact for programme and venue qualification. The official contact page publishes andres@img.org.mx. No procurement mandate or hotel-signing authority is established.

recommended_next_step.title: Recommended next step
recommended_next_step.body: Reclassify 2026 as a past, named-venue programme and open a conditional March 2027 prospect. Send a short, transparent hotel-supplier introduction to Leticia Limón, copying Andrés Franco, asking who owns accommodation/venue sourcing and whether bids for the 2027 Cancún congress are welcome. If sourcing is open, offer a nonbinding residential-meeting proposal or site inspection covering single/double occupancy, meal inclusions, plenary space, AV and accessible arrangements. Request actual historical pickup and the 2027 brief before quoting or forecasting. Separate paid hospitality terms from any optional, documented sponsorship; do not offer personal benefits to officials or imply privileged access to public contracts.
qualificationQuestions: What are the exact March 2027 dates, and is Grand Oasis retained or is venue sourcing open?
Who owns programme logistics, hotel selection and procurement, and who may sign the hotel agreement?
Which legal entity will contract and pay, and can it provide current fiscal identification and signatory authority?
Will IMG buy a master block, will delegates book individually, or will municipalities or an intermediary pay?
What plenary capacity, stage, AV, interpretation, breakout rooms and working hours are required?
Which meals are covered by all-inclusive service, and are private functions, coffee breaks or banquets required?
What budget approval, quotation/tender process, vendor registration, invoice and payment requirements apply to each payer?

facts: Latest activity evidence found: a report published 16 October 2026 describes the chapter’s monthly meeting under D’eniss Montiel, including an activity report, business alliances, new members and member-benefit agreements. It does not identify the venue or exact event date.

An April 2026 monthly meeting was reported at Renaissance Cancún Resort & Marina, including an activity report, alternative-dispute-resolution content, training/development and a member-business presentation.

The 18 June 2026 monthly breakfast took place at Hotel Renaissance Cancún. Reporting records 07:50 registration and an 11:00 close, with institutional reporting and talks on entrepreneurial resilience, financial protection and AI/cybersecurity.

Competitor venue evidence: Renaissance Cancún Resort & Marina is the strongest repeated-use benchmark for the monthly programme. Presidente InterContinental hosted a monthly breakfast and assembly reported in August 2024. Secrets The Vine Cancun hosted the September 2026 board swearing-in, a separate ceremonial event rather than proof of a regular breakfast booking.

The municipality’s 22 September 2026 announcement identifies D’eniss Montiel Cruz as president for 2026–2029, with Paloma Ceballos as secretary and Eva Algard Padrón as treasurer; the chapter’s own 2026 board page also lists these roles. Mirian Esther Escalante Rejón is the outgoing president, not the current primary sales target.

The hotel’s official meetings material advertises indoor meeting space, breakout facilities, outdoor event areas and a banquet menu. María Fernanda has 20 banquet places; individual Península sections are listed at 60 banquet places in the official property presentation. These are room capacities, not AMEXME attendance.
uncertainties: No future breakfast date, 2027 calendar, fixed day-of-month, guaranteed annual event count or venue procurement cycle verified.
No reliable programme attendance, budget, catering spend, sponsor contribution or contracted revenue verified.
No confirmed contracting authority, dedicated event planner, incumbent exclusivity, venue renewal date or open request for proposals.
Breakfast-only non-resident access, minimum spend, day-pass obligations, parking and final room configuration require hotel confirmation.
The October report establishes recent continuity but does not establish its venue or exact meeting date. Publication dates must not be substituted for event dates.
No guestroom demand established; chapter meetings must not be conflated with the separate national congress.

commercialIntelligenceBrief.recommendedNextStep: First have the hotel confirm a viable non-resident breakfast-only offer. Then email chapter coordination, addressed to D’eniss Montiel, referencing the documented June breakfast and October monthly session. Request a short qualification call with the actual venue buyer and ask for the next uncommitted monthly date plus the following quarter’s calendar. Offer a site inspection and one pilot morning, using the June event’s 07:50 registration and 11:00 close as a discussion template, not an assumed recurring timetable. Quote two transparent options: breakfast plus private room, and breakfast plus an extended training/coffee-break session; separate included equipment from paid AV and access charges. Right-size the room to the guaranteed count. Position the pilot as a comparison with the repeatedly used Renaissance venue on total attendee cost, privacy, service and arrival convenience. Only after a successful pilot seek a repeat-date agreement; do not assume an incumbent contract is available to displace.

facts_and_uncertainties.title: Established facts and uncertainties
facts: Latest activity evidence found: a report published 16 October 2026 describes the chapter’s monthly meeting under D’eniss Montiel, including an activity report, business alliances, new members and member-benefit agreements. It does not identify the venue or exact event date.

An April 2026 monthly meeting was reported at Renaissance Cancún Resort & Marina, including an activity report, alternative-dispute-resolution content, training/development and a member-business presentation.

The 18 June 2026 monthly breakfast took place at Hotel Renaissance Cancún. Reporting records 07:50 registration and an 11:00 close, with institutional reporting and talks on entrepreneurial resilience, financial protection and AI/cybersecurity.

Competitor venue evidence: Renaissance Cancún Resort & Marina is the strongest repeated-use benchmark for the monthly programme. Presidente InterContinental hosted a monthly breakfast and assembly reported in August 2024. Secrets The Vine Cancun hosted the September 2026 board swearing-in, a separate ceremonial event rather than proof of a regular breakfast booking.

The municipality’s 22 September 2026 announcement identifies D’eniss Montiel Cruz as president for 2026–2029, with Paloma Ceballos as secretary and Eva Algard Padrón as treasurer; the chapter’s own 2026 board page also lists these roles. Mirian Esther Escalante Rejón is the outgoing president, not the current primary sales target.

The hotel’s official meetings material advertises indoor meeting space, breakout facilities, outdoor event areas and a banquet menu. María Fernanda has 20 banquet places; individual Península sections are listed at 60 banquet places in the official property presentation. These are room capacities, not AMEXME attendance.
uncertainties: No future breakfast date, 2027 calendar, fixed day-of-month, guaranteed annual event count or venue procurement cycle verified.
No reliable programme attendance, budget, catering spend, sponsor contribution or contracted revenue verified.
No confirmed contracting authority, dedicated event planner, incumbent exclusivity, venue renewal date or open request for proposals.
Breakfast-only non-resident access, minimum spend, day-pass obligations, parking and final room configuration require hotel confirmation.
The October report establishes recent continuity but does not establish its venue or exact meeting date. Publication dates must not be substituted for event dates.
No guestroom demand established; chapter meetings must not be conflated with the separate national congress.

recommended_next_step.title: Recommended next step
recommended_next_step.body: First have the hotel confirm a viable non-resident breakfast-only offer. Then email chapter coordination, addressed to D’eniss Montiel, referencing the documented June breakfast and October monthly session. Request a short qualification call with the actual venue buyer and ask for the next uncommitted monthly date plus the following quarter’s calendar. Offer a site inspection and one pilot morning, using the June event’s 07:50 registration and 11:00 close as a discussion template, not an assumed recurring timetable. Quote two transparent options: breakfast plus private room, and breakfast plus an extended training/coffee-break session; separate included equipment from paid AV and access charges. Right-size the room to the guaranteed count. Position the pilot as a comparison with the repeatedly used Renaissance venue on total attendee cost, privacy, service and arrival convenience. Only after a successful pilot seek a repeat-date agreement; do not assume an incumbent contract is available to displace.
qualificationQuestions: Who coordinates these breakfasts, chooses venues, approves expenditure and signs the agreement?
What are the next uncontracted dates, booking lead time and usual monthly scheduling rule? Are venues rotated or subject to an existing agreement?
Is breakfast paid centrally, through individual tickets, by a sponsor, or through member subscriptions? What is the acceptable all-in per-attendee ceiling?
Which inclusions and commercial terms does the current Renaissance arrangement provide, and what would justify a Hotel Zone venue change?
Does the hotel allow meeting-only non-resident entry without a room booking or full day pass, and what access, parking and accessibility provisions apply?
What presentation, sound, Wi-Fi, dietary, invoicing, deposit and cancellation requirements must the proposal cover?
Would a one-off breakfast pilot be useful, and which sessions could extend into a paid training break or working lunch?

potential_business.title: Potential business for this hotel
potential_business.body: Qualified local catering/day-meeting prospect for Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive, conditional on non-resident pricing and access. Renaissance Cancún repeatedly hosted the programme, demonstrating real hotel-based demand rather than inferred resort incentive demand. The resort offers dedicated meetings infrastructure and banquet service: María Fernanda accommodates 20 banquet or 12 classroom; the official property presentation lists individual Península sections at 60 banquet or 40 classroom. Select the space only after confirming attendance and allowing for speakers, registration and AV. Sell a private business breakfast and productive morning, not an overnight all-inclusive leisure package. The Hotel Zone setting must justify its convenience against the existing venue; no attendance volume or conversion probability is established.

facts_and_uncertainties.title: Established facts and uncertainties
facts: Latest activity evidence found: a report published 16 October 2026 describes the chapter’s monthly meeting under D’eniss Montiel, including an activity report, business alliances, new members and member-benefit agreements. It does not identify the venue or exact event date.

An April 2026 monthly meeting was reported at Renaissance Cancún Resort & Marina, including an activity report, alternative-dispute-resolution content, training/development and a member-business presentation.

The 18 June 2026 monthly breakfast took place at Hotel Renaissance Cancún. Reporting records 07:50 registration and an 11:00 close, with institutional reporting and talks on entrepreneurial resilience, financial protection and AI/cybersecurity.

Competitor venue evidence: Renaissance Cancún Resort & Marina is the strongest repeated-use benchmark for the monthly programme. Presidente InterContinental hosted a monthly breakfast and assembly reported in August 2024. Secrets The Vine Cancun hosted the September 2026 board swearing-in, a separate ceremonial event rather than proof of a regular breakfast booking.

The municipality’s 22 September 2026 announcement identifies D’eniss Montiel Cruz as president for 2026–2029, with Paloma Ceballos as secretary and Eva Algard Padrón as treasurer; the chapter’s own 2026 board page also lists these roles. Mirian Esther Escalante Rejón is the outgoing president, not the current primary sales target.

The hotel’s official meetings material advertises indoor meeting space, breakout facilities, outdoor event areas and a banquet menu. María Fernanda has 20 banquet places; individual Península sections are listed at 60 banquet places in the official property presentation. These are room capacities, not AMEXME attendance.
uncertainties: No future breakfast date, 2027 calendar, fixed day-of-month, guaranteed annual event count or venue procurement cycle verified.
No reliable programme attendance, budget, catering spend, sponsor contribution or contracted revenue verified.
No confirmed contracting authority, dedicated event planner, incumbent exclusivity, venue renewal date or open request for proposals.
Breakfast-only non-resident access, minimum spend, day-pass obligations, parking and final room configuration require hotel confirmation.
The October report establishes recent continuity but does not establish its venue or exact meeting date. Publication dates must not be substituted for event dates.
No guestroom demand established; chapter meetings must not be conflated with the separate national congress.

recommended_next_step.title: Recommended next step
recommended_next_step.body: First have the hotel confirm a viable non-resident breakfast-only offer. Then email chapter coordination, addressed to D’eniss Montiel, referencing the documented June breakfast and October monthly session. Request a short qualification call with the actual venue buyer and ask for the next uncommitted monthly date plus the following quarter’s calendar. Offer a site inspection and one pilot morning, using the June event’s 07:50 registration and 11:00 close as a discussion template, not an assumed recurring timetable. Quote two transparent options: breakfast plus private room, and breakfast plus an extended training/coffee-break session; separate included equipment from paid AV and access charges. Right-size the room to the guaranteed count. Position the pilot as a comparison with the repeatedly used Renaissance venue on total attendee cost, privacy, service and arrival convenience. Only after a successful pilot seek a repeat-date agreement; do not assume an incumbent contract is available to displace.
qualificationQuestions: Who coordinates these breakfasts, chooses venues, approves expenditure and signs the agreement?
What are the next uncontracted dates, booking lead time and usual monthly scheduling rule? Are venues rotated or subject to an existing agreement?
Is breakfast paid centrally, through individual tickets, by a sponsor, or through member subscriptions? What is the acceptable all-in per-attendee ceiling?
Which inclusions and commercial terms does the current Renaissance arrangement provide, and what would justify a Hotel Zone venue change?
Does the hotel allow meeting-only non-resident entry without a room booking or full day pass, and what access, parking and accessibility provisions apply?
What presentation, sound, Wi-Fi, dietary, invoicing, deposit and cancellation requirements must the proposal cover?
Would a one-off breakfast pilot be useful, and which sessions could extend into a paid training break or working lunch?

facts: The 15 August 2025 municipal release advertises free courses on team management, wellbeing, gender violence and ARCO data-protection rights, using Zoom or Moodle for the listed sessions.

The January 2026 municipal calendar includes both online and classroom activity. Conversational English was scheduled from 19 January to 6 March, Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, 09:30–11:00, at the department’s Avenida Nader classroom.

The 5 October 2026 municipal announcement schedules online courses on 20, 22 and 29 October; classroom English from 5 October to 27 November; and basic first aid on 27–28 October, 10:00–12:00, at the Academia de Bomberos on Avenida Tulum. These are advertised schedules, not independent proof that every session occurred.

Frequency is recurring monthly programming, with individual short workshops and multiweek language cohorts. The published January language cycle demonstrates multiple sessions per week, not a hotel booking cycle.

A 24 September 2026 El Momento report attributes 71 courses and 1,888 participants during April–June 2026 to the department’s quarterly report. This is secondary-source delivery evidence; the underlying primary report was not located, and these totals are not hotel attendance or unique hotel customers.
The hotel officially markets 12 meeting rooms, approximately 2,000 square metres of event space, and a planning/catering team. María Fernanda provides a specifically evidenced small-room option.
The municipal directory names both Romina Cervera Estrella in Capacitación en Calidad and Angélica Leticia Bote Pacheco in Recursos Materiales.

Adhara Cancún markets corporate meeting configurations and breakfast/coffee-break/meal menus. Wyndham Grand Cancún markets seven event rooms, catering and coffee breaks. Neither was verified as an ICCAL customer venue.
uncertainties: No hotel booking, external-venue request, catering purchase, procurement notice or paid hospitality budget for this programme was verified.
Future external-venue dates, cohort sizes, frequency of paid hotel use and decision deadlines remain unknown.
No evidence establishes ICCAL use of Fiesta Americana Condesa, Adhara or Wyndham Grand; competitor suitability is inferred from their own event offerings.
The current operating name is documented, but the legal instrument or date changing the historical ICCAL structure was not verified.
Contracting authority, purchasing route, funding eligibility, payment terms and any permissible sponsorship arrangement require direct confirmation.
The resort’s meeting-only admission policy, minimum spend, available dates, prices, accessible meeting route and transport practicality remain unverified.

opportunities.whyThisHotel: Conditional, low-priority local day-meeting prospect; not a qualified recurring hotel account. In-person activity is established, but October 2026 courses use the department’s Avenida Nader classroom and the Academia de Bomberos, while other sessions are online. Fiesta Americana Condesa has appropriate small-meeting infrastructure: María Fernanda accommodates 12 classroom-style, 16 at an imperial table, or 24 theatre-style, with air-conditioning and a screen. Its resort setting could differentiate an occasional instructor workshop or employer-sponsored training day, but does not establish demand for incentives or overnight stays. The commercial hurdle is persuading an identified payer that an external Hotel Zone venue adds value over existing municipal facilities. Monthly programming must not be converted into assumed monthly hotel bookings.
whyThisHotelAdvantages: Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive sits in the same commercial market as the documented programme activity.
whyThisHotelLimitations: No verified hotel booking, RFP, or preferred-supplier agreement is established from public research alone.
opportunities.whyNow: The verified recurring lunch programme creates a legitimate opening to approach organizers about future venue rotations, pilot breakfast/lunch dates, or overflow requirements. No verified open sourcing window or next bookable date after the research cut-off has been established — treat as active monitoring, not urgent displacement of the incumbent.
establishedFacts: The 15 August 2025 municipal release advertises free courses on team management, wellbeing, gender violence and ARCO data-protection rights, using Zoom or Moodle for the listed sessions.

The January 2026 municipal calendar includes both online and classroom activity. Conversational English was scheduled from 19 January to 6 March, Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, 09:30–11:00, at the department’s Avenida Nader classroom.

The 5 October 2026 municipal announcement schedules online courses on 20, 22 and 29 October; classroom English from 5 October to 27 November; and basic first aid on 27–28 October, 10:00–12:00, at the Academia de Bomberos on Avenida Tulum. These are advertised schedules, not independent proof that every session occurred.

Frequency is recurring monthly programming, with individual short workshops and multiweek language cohorts. The published January language cycle demonstrates multiple sessions per week, not a hotel booking cycle.

A 24 September 2026 El Momento report attributes 71 courses and 1,888 participants during April–June 2026 to the department’s quarterly report. This is secondary-source delivery evidence; the underlying primary report was not located, and these totals are not hotel attendance or unique hotel customers.
The hotel officially markets 12 meeting rooms, approximately 2,000 square metres of event space, and a planning/catering team. María Fernanda provides a specifically evidenced small-room option.
The municipal directory names both Romina Cervera Estrella in Capacitación en Calidad and Angélica Leticia Bote Pacheco in Recursos Materiales.

Adhara Cancún markets corporate meeting configurations and breakfast/coffee-break/meal menus. Wyndham Grand Cancún markets seven event rooms, catering and coffee breaks. Neither was verified as an ICCAL customer venue.
uncertainties: No hotel booking, external-venue request, catering purchase, procurement notice or paid hospitality budget for this programme was verified.
Future external-venue dates, cohort sizes, frequency of paid hotel use and decision deadlines remain unknown.
No evidence establishes ICCAL use of Fiesta Americana Condesa, Adhara or Wyndham Grand; competitor suitability is inferred from their own event offerings.
The current operating name is documented, but the legal instrument or date changing the historical ICCAL structure was not verified.
Contracting authority, purchasing route, funding eligibility, payment terms and any permissible sponsorship arrangement require direct confirmation.
The resort’s meeting-only admission policy, minimum spend, available dates, prices, accessible meeting route and transport practicality remain unverified.

what_is_happening.title: What is happening
what_is_happening.body: ALAT held its four-day respiratory-health congress 9–12 July 2025 in Cancún at Cancún Center, with international faculty, professional sessions, exhibition-capable space and published accommodation arrangements. This is verified convention demand with clear room, meeting, exhibition, catering and event-production relevance.

potential_business.title: Potential business for this hotel
potential_business.body: Retain as historical meetings/congress demand; do not qualify it as relocation or extended stay. The verified travel mechanism was attendance by respiratory-health professionals, international faculty and presenting researchers, with a specific scholarship pathway offering selected researchers three nights of shared lodging. There is no verified employer assignment, employee transfer, construction deployment or permanent-housing requirement. Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive has a plausible short-stay resort-group fit for delegates, faculty or accompanying guests and optional private functions, not a demonstrated residential-placement fit. The hotel advertises 12 event rooms and group lodging packages, but the congress venue was Cancún Center, not this resort. Cancún Center is at Boulevard Kukulcán km 9 and the hotel at km 16.5: venue transport would need qualification; do not sell it as an on-site congress hotel. Any pre/post leisure extension remains a sales hypothesis. The announced 2027 congress is in San José, Costa Rica, so annual ALAT recurrence does not establish recurring Cancún demand.

why_this_hotel.title: Why this hotel
advantages: Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive is commercially positioned against the evidenced activity geography — evaluate as an alternative or overflow venue, not a confirmed booking.
limitations: No verified hotel booking, RFP, or preferred-supplier agreement is established from public research alone.

why_act_now.title: Why act now
why_act_now.body: Historical expansion or mobility signals may justify a qualified outreach to mobility/HR contacts, but no verified future inbound assignment cohort or temporary-lodging RFP has been established. Do not invent urgency from employment-expansion headlines.

facts_and_uncertainties.title: Established facts and uncertainties
facts: The official congress site identifies 9–12 July 2025 in Cancún and describes international faculty and four days of respiratory-health scientific exchange.
Cancún Center was the congress venue; the official venue page gives Boulevard Kukulcán km 9, Punta Cancún, Hotel Zone.

Official abstract rules required an author or another investigator to register and attend to present an accepted paper, establishing a concrete attendance trigger rather than an employment assignment.
Official rules offered the two best free papers of each department registration and three nights of shared accommodation for the 2025 congress.
Turenlaces advertised accommodation and breakfast for 8–13 July 2025, explicitly five nights/six days, with airport transfers and travel insurance.
The official congress homepage linked a dedicated accommodation portal; the portal’s contents were not verified.
The subject resort advertises 12 event rooms, indoor/outdoor group spaces, planning support and packages including lodging; its homepage lists an Accessible Room.
ALAT’s current executive page identifies Lorena Noriega Aguirre as president for 2026–2028 and lists general coordination, operations, finance and congress commercial staff.
ALAT announces the 20th congress for 7–10 July 2027 in San José, Costa Rica, at Centro de Convenciones de Costa Rica, with Hacienda Belén de Marriott as host hotel.
uncertainties: No verified employer assignment mechanism, relocation programme, HR/mobility owner, construction deployment or permanent-housing need.
No verified 2025 ALAT contract, preferred-hotel status, room block or realised guestroom production at Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún.
Actual stay lengths, scholarship redemptions, delegate volumes, room nights, budgets and authorised signatories remain unknown.
The official housing portal’s operator, hotel inventory, commercial terms and booking outcomes remain unverified; third-party offers do not resolve these.
No future Cancún congress or related extended assignment was established; recurrence elsewhere is not recurring local demand.
Accessible-room inventory/features and venue transfer arrangements require direct confirmation.

recommended_next_step.title: Recommended next step
recommended_next_step.body: Remove this 2025 event from active relocation/extended-stay pipeline and retain it as a historical congress/account-development lead. Start with Gustavo Giraldo and Victoria Baldi to identify the actual 2025 housing coordinator and whether any future Cancún meetings or faculty visits are planned. Request historical hotel participation and stay-length evidence only if useful for account qualification; do not propose a live 2025 room block. The announced next congress is 7–10 July 2027 in San José, with Hacienda Belén de Marriott named as host hotel, so it is not a room-demand anchor for this Cancún resort. Route any independently verified future Cancún congress requirement to meetings/group sales. Coordinate with Projects (Seg 7) only if a separate construction-led deployment is subsequently evidenced; nothing found makes construction the principal mechanism here.
qualificationQuestions: Who managed the 2025 accommodation portal, selected hotels and held any hotel agreements?
Was Fiesta Americana Condesa included, and is there evidence of actual bookings or pickup there?
Were delegate, invited-faculty, award-recipient and organiser rooms booked separately, and who paid for each?
What were actual arrival/departure patterns and shared-room arrangements, distinct from the advertised three-night award and five-night agency package?
Did any staff or faculty stay beyond the congress for a documented temporary assignment? If so, what role, assignment dates and expected duration applied?
Is there any genuine employee relocation or permanent-housing search, or is the requirement exclusively temporary event lodging?
Who is the authorised accommodation buyer and signatory, and which agency, sponsor or institution controls payment?
Are any future Cancún events confirmed independently of the 2027 Costa Rica congress?

opportunities.guestroomDemandStatus: Historical temporary hotel lodging is verified: a three-night minimum package, ROH deluxe rooms with sea or mangrove views allocated by Hilton according to availability, and a group rate available three days before or after the core dates. These optional short extensions are not proof of extended-stay work assignments. Official marketing targeted more than 1,000 women entrepreneurs; contemporaneous reporting described around 1,000 participants. Neither figure establishes occupied rooms or room nights. Off-property attendance through a Congress Pass was permitted. No room pickup, current Fiesta Americana booking, permanent housing, residential lease, employee relocation entitlement or recurring long-stay roster was verified.

what_is_happening.title: What is happening
what_is_happening.body: AMEXME held its 27–30 August 2025 national congress at Hilton Cancun for more than 1,000 women entrepreneurs. The published all-inclusive programme included airport transfers, hotel welcome and closing dinners, an off-site themed dinner, coffee breaks, business sessions, networking and a commercial area—strong resort group, banquet and meeting demand evidence.

potential_business.title: Potential business for this hotel
potential_business.body: Strong product-category fit, but no verified current demand for Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive. The documented mechanism is attendee registration and a congress hotel package, not employer-directed relocation, staff rotation or construction deployment. Resort guestrooms, meeting sessions, networking, banquets and leisure extensions align with this beachfront all-inclusive hotel and its 12 event rooms. This is a meetings-and-groups prospect, not a qualified relocation account. The 2025 host was Hilton, not the subject property; do not infer overflow or a room block at Fiesta Americana. The official 2026 congress page named Acapulco, and the 2027 congress is already advertised at Hacienda del Mar Los Cabos, 26–28 May 2027. A future Cancún opportunity must therefore be separately qualified.

facts: The environmental filing names Tren Maya, S.A. de C.V. as promoter and includes locomotive facilities, administrative functions, Guardia Nacional accommodation and crew accommodation.

The MIA’s temporary-works section expressly proposes a camp and site hut for field brigades, says accommodated personnel will rotate, and describes a mobile camp for temporary management, supervision, administration and logistics. This is planned on-site accommodation, not proof of an operating camp or hotel bookings.

The planned Guardia Nacional facility accommodates 24 personnel and a commander on a rotating basis. Planned crew accommodation temporarily shelters 40 male/female crew members passing through the terminal. These are design capacities, not hotel-room requirements.

Permanent terminal buildings can provide temporary occupancy: crew transit lodging and rotating Guardia Nacional quarters are not evidence of family relocation or permanent residential housing. The construction camp is itself temporary infrastructure.
The MIA projects 18 months of site preparation/construction and 50 years of operation/maintenance; individual assignment durations are not stated.
The official project tracker reports 67.97% progress in September 2026 for first-phase freight infrastructure across four complexes, including Cancún. This is not a Cancún-only progress figure.
The hotel’s official pages describe an all-inclusive beachfront product with Wi-Fi, restaurants and meeting facilities; the meetings page lists 507 rooms/suites and 12 breakout rooms.
uncertainties: Current camp availability, occupancy and completion of operational accommodation are not verified; planned facilities should not be treated as occupied beds.
No terminal-specific external lodging contract, hotel block, assignment roster, individual stay duration, room-night volume, lodging budget or contracting authority was verified.
No dedicated mobility manager was verified. The named HR lead appears in an illustrative annex and requires current-role confirmation; operator contacts may not control construction lodging.
The exact Cancún commissioning sequence remains unresolved: public milestones concern different scopes, from initial facilities to the full freight system.
Hotel kitchens/kitchenettes, laundry provision, workforce suitability, negotiated long-stay terms and daily terminal shuttle were not established by the reviewed official hotel pages.
No permanent-home relocation programme, family move, residential lease requirement or guaranteed resort incentive demand is evidenced.

facts_and_uncertainties.title: Established facts and uncertainties
facts: The environmental filing names Tren Maya, S.A. de C.V. as promoter and includes locomotive facilities, administrative functions, Guardia Nacional accommodation and crew accommodation.

The MIA’s temporary-works section expressly proposes a camp and site hut for field brigades, says accommodated personnel will rotate, and describes a mobile camp for temporary management, supervision, administration and logistics. This is planned on-site accommodation, not proof of an operating camp or hotel bookings.

The planned Guardia Nacional facility accommodates 24 personnel and a commander on a rotating basis. Planned crew accommodation temporarily shelters 40 male/female crew members passing through the terminal. These are design capacities, not hotel-room requirements.

Permanent terminal buildings can provide temporary occupancy: crew transit lodging and rotating Guardia Nacional quarters are not evidence of family relocation or permanent residential housing. The construction camp is itself temporary infrastructure.
The MIA projects 18 months of site preparation/construction and 50 years of operation/maintenance; individual assignment durations are not stated.
The official project tracker reports 67.97% progress in September 2026 for first-phase freight infrastructure across four complexes, including Cancún. This is not a Cancún-only progress figure.
The hotel’s official pages describe an all-inclusive beachfront product with Wi-Fi, restaurants and meeting facilities; the meetings page lists 507 rooms/suites and 12 breakout rooms.
uncertainties: Current camp availability, occupancy and completion of operational accommodation are not verified; planned facilities should not be treated as occupied beds.
No terminal-specific external lodging contract, hotel block, assignment roster, individual stay duration, room-night volume, lodging budget or contracting authority was verified.
No dedicated mobility manager was verified. The named HR lead appears in an illustrative annex and requires current-role confirmation; operator contacts may not control construction lodging.
The exact Cancún commissioning sequence remains unresolved: public milestones concern different scopes, from initial facilities to the full freight system.
Hotel kitchens/kitchenettes, laundry provision, workforce suitability, negotiated long-stay terms and daily terminal shuttle were not established by the reviewed official hotel pages.
No permanent-home relocation programme, family move, residential lease requirement or guaranteed resort incentive demand is evidenced.

qualificationQuestions: Which entity employs and deploys each cohort: military construction organisation, contractor, equipment supplier or Tren Maya operations?
Who is the Cancún site HR/logistics administrator, who books lodging, who pays, and who is authorized to approve the procurement?
Which temporary camps and terminal accommodation buildings are commissioned and occupied today, and which personnel are eligible to use them?
Is any off-site accommodation required because of capacity, policy, specialist status or commissioning timing? What dated roster supports that requirement?
What are the individual assignment dates, rotation cycle, stay length and extension/cancellation conditions, distinct from the construction schedule?
Are personnel temporarily assigned, commuting locally, or transferring permanently with dependants? Is any request for interim hotel lodging before a residential lease?
What is the latest Cancún-specific construction, testing and operational handover calendar?
What purchasing procedure, supplier registration, invoicing requirements, travel limits and accommodation policy apply to the actual payer?

what_is_happening.title: What is happening
what_is_happening.body: The official environmental filing describes construction of a Cancún rail-freight terminal near the airport, including locomotive facilities, administrative functions, Guardia Nacional accommodation and crew accommodation. The 2025–2026 freight-infrastructure programme supports a credible rotating construction, commissioning and rail-operations demand signal near the airport corridor.

potential_business.title: Potential business for this hotel
potential_business.body: Conditional, secondary opportunity for Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive—not a qualified base-load extended-stay account. The environmental filing explicitly plans a temporary camp for rotating field brigades, plus separate terminal accommodation for Guardia Nacional and crews. These provisions weaken any assumption that deployed personnel require commercial guestrooms. The beachfront all-inclusive resort and its meeting facilities are better aligned with potential short executive, supplier or commissioning visits and residential briefings/training than routine workforce housing; no such bookings are established. Meals and Wi-Fi could support visiting teams, but the Hotel Zone location is not the terminal site. Validate the actual gate-to-hotel commute, shift transport, laundry, work-compatible meal times, rate acceptability and long-stay conditions before proposing accommodation. No room nights, spend or conversion probability can be substantiated.

why_this_hotel.title: Why this hotel
why_this_hotel.body: Conditional, secondary opportunity for Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive—not a qualified base-load extended-stay account. The environmental filing explicitly plans a temporary camp for rotating field brigades, plus separate terminal accommodation for Guardia Nacional and crews. These provisions weaken any assumption that deployed personnel require commercial guestrooms. The beachfront all-inclusive resort and its meeting facilities are better aligned with potential short executive, supplier or commissioning visits and residential briefings/training than routine workforce housing; no such bookings are established. Meals and Wi-Fi could support visiting teams, but the Hotel Zone location is not the terminal site. advantages: Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive is commercially positioned against the evidenced activity geography — evaluate as an alternative or overflow venue, not a confirmed booking.
limitations: No verified hotel booking, RFP, or preferred-supplier agreement is established from public research alone.

why_act_now.title: Why act now
why_act_now.body: Historical expansion or mobility signals may justify a qualified outreach to mobility/HR contacts, but no verified future inbound assignment cohort or temporary-lodging RFP has been established. Do not invent urgency from employment-expansion headlines.

facts_and_uncertainties.title: Established facts and uncertainties
facts: The environmental filing names Tren Maya, S.A. de C.V. as promoter and includes locomotive facilities, administrative functions, Guardia Nacional accommodation and crew accommodation.

The MIA’s temporary-works section expressly proposes a camp and site hut for field brigades, says accommodated personnel will rotate, and describes a mobile camp for temporary management, supervision, administration and logistics. This is planned on-site accommodation, not proof of an operating camp or hotel bookings.

The planned Guardia Nacional facility accommodates 24 personnel and a commander on a rotating basis. Planned crew accommodation temporarily shelters 40 male/female crew members passing through the terminal. These are design capacities, not hotel-room requirements.

Permanent terminal buildings can provide temporary occupancy: crew transit lodging and rotating Guardia Nacional quarters are not evidence of family relocation or permanent residential housing. The construction camp is itself temporary infrastructure.
The MIA projects 18 months of site preparation/construction and 50 years of operation/maintenance; individual assignment durations are not stated.
The official project tracker reports 67.97% progress in September 2026 for first-phase freight infrastructure across four complexes, including Cancún. This is not a Cancún-only progress figure.
The hotel’s official pages describe an all-inclusive beachfront product with Wi-Fi, restaurants and meeting facilities; the meetings page lists 507 rooms/suites and 12 breakout rooms.
uncertainties: Current camp availability, occupancy and completion of operational accommodation are not verified; planned facilities should not be treated as occupied beds.
No terminal-specific external lodging contract, hotel block, assignment roster, individual stay duration, room-night volume, lodging budget or contracting authority was verified.
No dedicated mobility manager was verified. The named HR lead appears in an illustrative annex and requires current-role confirmation; operator contacts may not control construction lodging.
The exact Cancún commissioning sequence remains unresolved: public milestones concern different scopes, from initial facilities to the full freight system.
Hotel kitchens/kitchenettes, laundry provision, workforce suitability, negotiated long-stay terms and daily terminal shuttle were not established by the reviewed official hotel pages.
No permanent-home relocation programme, family move, residential lease requirement or guaranteed resort incentive demand is evidenced.

Ask which entity buys temporary lodging and who owns supplier onboarding; this does not establish his authority over the construction workforce or a hotel contract.
