recommended_next_step.title: Recommended next step
recommended_next_step.body: Route to Projects (Seg 7) as a construction-deployment lead, not a confirmed relocation account. Jointly approach operator procurement/HR to identify the Cancún site administrator, construction employer, commissioning contractors and actual lodging payer. First establish whether camp/terminal beds cover all personnel and whether any named off-site cohort exists. If yes, obtain dates, rotation lengths, approval route and transport requirements, then ask hotel sales to assess a compliant project-stay offer. Pursue executive visits or residential meetings only against a defined requirement. If accommodation is fully provided on site, retain as a monitored project rather than forecast guestrooms.
qualificationQuestions: Which entity employs and deploys each cohort: military construction organisation, contractor, equipment supplier or Tren Maya operations?
Who is the Cancún site HR/logistics administrator, who books lodging, who pays, and who is authorized to approve the procurement?
Which temporary camps and terminal accommodation buildings are commissioned and occupied today, and which personnel are eligible to use them?
Is any off-site accommodation required because of capacity, policy, specialist status or commissioning timing? What dated roster supports that requirement?
What are the individual assignment dates, rotation cycle, stay length and extension/cancellation conditions, distinct from the construction schedule?
Are personnel temporarily assigned, commuting locally, or transferring permanently with dependants? Is any request for interim hotel lodging before a residential lease?
What is the latest Cancún-specific construction, testing and operational handover calendar?
What purchasing procedure, supplier registration, invoicing requirements, travel limits and accommodation policy apply to the actual payer?

commercialIntelligenceBrief.potentialBusinessForThisHotel: Conditional, secondary prospect—not an unmet-lodging-gap lead. The prior discovery note understates the lodging integration: Aloft Cancún is directly connected to the convention center and the venue promotes its 177 rooms. For Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive, the credible proposition is an optional all-inclusive beach-resort block for multi-day congress delegates, incentive-linked groups, accompanying families or pre/post-event leisure extensions, rather than the closest default congress hotel. Its 507 rooms, beach setting, group services and 12 meeting rooms support a proposed accommodation-plus-private-breakout or retreat offer. Those segments are a fit hypothesis, not demonstrated venue referrals. Condesa’s Km 16.5 address versus the venue’s Km 9 address makes transport a material qualification item; no journey time is asserted. Prioritize only where organizers want a resort stay and accept a transport plan.

advantages: Multi-day international medical congresses provide a verified event-demand anchor more relevant to destination lodging than a generic local social-event listing.

Condesa’s official group materials publish 507 rooms, indoor and outdoor meeting areas, beach/pool/spa amenities and a dedicated groups-and-conventions team, supporting a differentiated resort-based stay.
The hotel explicitly offers event packages including lodging and special concessions; this provides a practical basis for a tailored proposal, without implying any existing Cancún Center agreement.

The venue already works through a hotel-and-services alliance, so lodging coordination is an established activity. Its current accommodation list also includes Canopy approximately 3 km away and Emporio approximately 8.2 km away, indicating that published options are not exclusively adjacent properties; this does not establish Condesa’s eligibility.
limitations: Directly connected Aloft and an established nearby hotel network reduce the strength of a new preferred-hotel pitch. ONSITE_LODGING_AVAILABLE refers to the connected hotel, not guestrooms inside the convention halls.

Grand Fiesta Americana Coral Beach is an existing listed alliance property and an ISAPS accommodation option opposite the convention center. It is not Fiesta Americana Condesa; brand similarity must not be mistaken for a Condesa relationship.
Condesa is not named on the reviewed official alliance accommodation list. No public evidence reviewed establishes an existing preferred-lodging agreement or referral flow for this property.

Transport between Condesa and the venue would need to be organized and costed. Venue-day catering plus the hotel’s all-inclusive meals may create a value-overlap objection for delegates away at sessions; this is a commercial risk to test, not a reported customer complaint.

Weddings, graduations, quinceañeras and year-end parties do not by themselves establish overnight demand. No verified attendee-origin mix, room nights, conversion rate, seasonal need or current block availability was found.

The Spanish venue homepage advertises a 4,701-room Punta Cancún network. This is a published marketing figure, not verified current bookable inventory or expected demand for Condesa.
The official alliance accommodation list names Grand Fiesta Americana Coral Beach, not Fiesta Americana Condesa; it also includes other hotel operators.
ISUOG 2025 and ISAPS 2026 organizer pages document multi-day congress programs at Cancún Center.
Condesa’s official meetings materials publish 507 rooms and suites and 12 breakout rooms; its property event page describes 12 event rooms and lodging-inclusive event packages.
uncertainties: No confirmed Condesa–Cancún Center preferred-lodging agreement, rates, commissions, exclusivity, organizer commitment or guaranteed room-night volume was found.
The 4,701-room network figure’s effective date and current inventory basis are not established; absence from a public member list is not proof that Condesa has no private commercial relationship.

Venue room dimensions and capacities differ across published pages; current certified capacities and usable layouts require direct confirmation.

Transfer duration/cost, attendee resort preference, future event availability and net incremental hotel revenue remain unverified.

potential_business.body: Conditional, secondary prospect—not an unmet-lodging-gap lead. The prior discovery note understates the lodging integration: Aloft Cancún is directly connected to the convention center and the venue promotes its 177 rooms. For Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive, the credible proposition is an optional all-inclusive beach-resort block for multi-day congress delegates, incentive-linked groups, accompanying families or pre/post-event leisure extensions, rather than the closest default congress hotel. Its 507 rooms, beach setting, group services and 12 meeting rooms support a proposed accommodation-plus-private-breakout or retreat offer. Those segments are a fit hypothesis, not demonstrated venue referrals. Condesa’s Km 16.5 address versus the venue’s Km 9 address makes transport a material qualification item; no journey time is asserted. Prioritize only where organizers want a resort stay and accept a transport plan.

facts_and_uncertainties.title: Established facts and uncertainties
facts: Cancún Center’s official address is at Boulevard Kukulkán Km 9 in Punta Cancún, within the Hotel Zone.

The venue promotes 177-room Aloft Cancún for lodging; the official alliance accommodation page explicitly says Aloft is directly connected to the convention center. Thus a categorical no-onsite-lodging assumption is not supported.
The Spanish venue homepage advertises a 4,701-room Punta Cancún network. This is a published marketing figure, not verified current bookable inventory or expected demand for Condesa.
The official alliance accommodation list names Grand Fiesta Americana Coral Beach, not Fiesta Americana Condesa; it also includes other hotel operators.
ISUOG 2025 and ISAPS 2026 organizer pages document multi-day congress programs at Cancún Center.
Condesa’s official meetings materials publish 507 rooms and suites and 12 breakout rooms; its property event page describes 12 event rooms and lodging-inclusive event packages.
uncertainties: No confirmed Condesa–Cancún Center preferred-lodging agreement, rates, commissions, exclusivity, organizer commitment or guaranteed room-night volume was found.
The 4,701-room network figure’s effective date and current inventory basis are not established; absence from a public member list is not proof that Condesa has no private commercial relationship.
The connected Aloft’s current block availability and the precise ownership/operating relationship between hotel and venue were not established.
Venue room dimensions and capacities differ across published pages; current certified capacities and usable layouts require direct confirmation.
David Solana’s current role is supported by his public professional profile, not an independently confirmed venue staff directory.
Transfer duration/cost, attendee resort preference, future event availability and net incremental hotel revenue remain unverified.

qualificationQuestions: Who selects official hotels and controls room blocks, attendee booking links and lodging referrals for each congress?
Can Fiesta Americana Condesa participate without alliance membership? Are there geographic, sponsorship, exclusivity or referral restrictions?
Which future events have unfilled accommodation needs, and what verified attendee-origin, stay-length and pickup data can organizers share?
Is there proven demand for an all-inclusive beach resort, accompanying-family stays or pre/post-congress extensions rather than accommodation within walking distance?
What room types, block sizes, arrival/departure patterns and accessibility requirements would an initial pilot need?
What shuttle schedule, accessibility standard and budget would organizers require, and who would contract and pay for transport?
How should all-inclusive inclusions be presented alongside convention-center meals, receptions and catering obligations?
Which party can approve the commercial terms, booking attribution, data permissions, cancellation/attrition provisions and any referral compensation?
Can the venue supply current dated floor plans and approved capacities for the specific event configuration?

Position Condesa as an optional all-inclusive resort/overflow or pre/post-stay option, not a replacement for Aloft or Coral Beach. First establish who controls accommodation selection—the venue, alliance, organizer or housing agency—and whether nonmember hotels can participate. If eligible, co-design one event-specific pilot with a defined room allocation, booking mechanism, transport proposal, cancellation terms and measurement of actual bookings. Do not propose an exclusive or volume-based agreement before the demand and decision rights are verified.
qualificationQuestions: Who selects official hotels and controls room blocks, attendee booking links and lodging referrals for each congress?
Can Fiesta Americana Condesa participate without alliance membership? Are there geographic, sponsorship, exclusivity or referral restrictions?
Which future events have unfilled accommodation needs, and what verified attendee-origin, stay-length and pickup data can organizers share?
Is there proven demand for an all-inclusive beach resort, accompanying-family stays or pre/post-congress extensions rather than accommodation within walking distance?
What room types, block sizes, arrival/departure patterns and accessibility requirements would an initial pilot need?
What shuttle schedule, accessibility standard and budget would organizers require, and who would contract and pay for transport?
How should all-inclusive inclusions be presented alongside convention-center meals, receptions and catering obligations?
Which party can approve the commercial terms, booking attribution, data permissions, cancellation/attrition provisions and any referral compensation?
Can the venue supply current dated floor plans and approved capacities for the specific event configuration?

commercialIntelligenceBrief.potentialBusinessForThisHotel: Conditional fit: pursue selected out-of-town speakers, performers, sponsors, executive delegations and attendees who want a beach-resort stay before or after an event—not undifferentiated local ticket buyers. Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive’s beach setting, lodging-inclusive group packages and 12 meeting rooms support a proposed combination of STOA’s staged program with resort lodging, smaller meetings or leisure extensions. This is a proposal, not an existing arrangement. The clearest lodging signal is historical and organizer-specific: published 2025 FIM guitar-competition rules explicitly discuss hotels, an official agency, preferential lodging/transfer offers and economical accommodation for participants and families. advantages: An operating event calendar includes professional-congress and ideas-conference formats, giving the hotel more targeted qualification opportunities than concerts alone.

limitations: No venue guestrooms or lodging operation are established by the reviewed facilities, rental and contact pages. UNKNOWN must not be converted to NO_ONSITE_LODGING without confirmation.

Published event capacities do not establish nonlocal attendance, room nights, stay length, booking conversion or year-round frequency.

Future event attendance, nonlocal share, actual accommodation purchases, lengths of stay and incremental hotel room-night opportunity are unquantified.
Existing preferred hotels, agency obligations, referral terms and any exclusivity remain unverified.
Resort budget acceptance and operational compatibility with full-day or evening off-site programming are untested.
Actual hotel–venue transfer logistics and the definitive approved capacity for a proposed layout remain to be confirmed.

These establish programming, not attendance, visitor origin or overnight demand.

potential_business.title: Potential business for this hotel
potential_business.body: Conditional fit: pursue selected out-of-town speakers, performers, sponsors, executive delegations and attendees who want a beach-resort stay before or after an event—not undifferentiated local ticket buyers. Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive’s beach setting, lodging-inclusive group packages and 12 meeting rooms support a proposed combination of STOA’s staged program with resort lodging, smaller meetings or leisure extensions. This is a proposal, not an existing arrangement. The clearest lodging signal is historical and organizer-specific: published 2025 FIM guitar-competition rules explicitly discuss hotels, an official agency, preferential lodging/transfer offers and economical accommodation for participants and families. That supports asking the organizer about room sourcing, but does not demonstrate resort-budget suitability, venue-controlled demand or a recurring account.

commercialIntelligenceBrief.potentialBusinessForThisHotel: Promising qualification-stage prospect for destination-wedding guest accommodation, rather than proven corporate or airport-corridor demand. The venue is at km 14.1 of Boulevard Kukulcan and the hotel is at km 16.5, placing both in the Hotel Zone without establishing a road distance or transfer time. Its explicit no-guest-lodging listing creates a plausible external room-block need, while Fiesta Americana Condesa offers an all-inclusive beach-resort stay for families, couples and groups. A photographer documents a wedding involving both this marina and Dreams Sands Cancún, supporting a multi-property event pattern but not proving any lodging agreement. Position Fiesta Americana Condesa as an accommodation option for couples already committed to the marina. The hotel also sells its own weddings, so clarify channel ownership and avoid competing for the same ceremony or reception. No partnership or room-night volume is established.

advantages: Explicit external-lodging opportunity: the venue’s wedding-directory profile answers No to guest accommodation; the official facilities list describes event spaces and dressing rooms rather than guestrooms.
Shared Hotel Zone setting supports a geographically coherent lodging proposition; actual transportation logistics still require validation.
Free supplier choice and venue-only rental suggest room to propose a separate hotel referral arrangement, but do not establish permission or willingness to do so.
Published 150-person overall capacity and documented destination-wedding activity make group accommodation worth qualifying; event attendance must not be treated as room demand.
The hotel explicitly welcomes families, couples and groups, aligning with wedding-party leisure stays rather than an unsupported city-center business-travel thesis.
limitations: Lodging evidence conflicts: Bodas.com.mx explicitly says no guest accommodation, while Aisle claims onsite rooms. The official venue site establishes only dressing rooms, not guestrooms. The classification follows the explicit venue-specific directory answer and should be confirmed in writing.
Published capacity is inconsistent: 150 overall versus 120 in the directory’s banquet FAQ. Layout-specific and weather-backup limits are unverified.
The hotel markets its own ceremonies, receptions, catering and guest stays; an external venue partnership could create sales-channel conflict.
Only three reserved parking spaces are listed on the official site; valet is extra. Coach access, loading, staging and late-night guest transfers require a site inspection.
Open-sided or partially covered event areas are described, but a fully enclosed weather contingency is not established.

No verified destination-guest share, room-block conversion, annual booking volume, existing hotel exclusivity, or corporate-event pipeline was found. Named contact leads are review-derived, with unverified titles.

qualificationQuestions: Do you have any overnight guestrooms, suites or affiliated accommodation, or are all bride/groom rooms strictly dressing facilities?
Who owns the venue and who can approve lodging referrals or preferred-hotel arrangements? Are Karla and Joceline current contacts, and what are their full names and roles?
Do any existing hotel, planner or agency agreements restrict referrals, exclusivity or guest accommodation choices?
For recent and forward-booked weddings, how many guests travel from outside Cancún, how many request lodging, and who selects and books their hotels?
What are typical requested stay lengths, booking lead times, family/child composition and accommodation budgets?
What are the current capacities for seated dinners, ceremonies and cocktails, and why do published limits differ between 120 and 150?
What usable covered capacity is available during rain or strong wind, and what cancellation or relocation procedures apply?
Can minibuses or coaches safely load and unload? What late-night pickup, accessibility, valet and vendor-access arrangements are permitted?
How would guest stays at an all-inclusive hotel work when the principal reception and dinner occur offsite, and what hotel services or ancillary events would guests actually want?
Would you accept a nonexclusive lodging-referral pilot, with agreed consent, lead handoff, booking attribution and pickup reporting, without promising unverified volumes?
Do you host corporate retreats, incentives or regional meetings? If so, can you provide recent examples and actual accommodation requirements?

The clearest opportunity is a lodging-only referral for out-of-town wedding and family-celebration guests who want a beachfront all-inclusive stay while celebrating at Casa Ambrosía. However, an urban Álamos event venue is not a Hotel Zone resort venue: the case depends on guests accepting the resort price proposition and separate event transfers. The hotel already markets its own weddings and meetings, so target genuinely incremental lodging rather than shifting hotel events off property.

Current ownership, trading status and operational policies have not been confirmed directly with management.

facts_and_uncertainties.title: Established facts and uncertainties
facts: EPIC was established in Cancún in 1988; its official website describes more than 35 years in the industry.
The official website markets MICE, destination management, weddings, transportation, tours and golf, including hotel negotiation/arrangements.
The official destination list includes Cancún and Riviera Maya, plus other Mexican beach and cultural destinations.
A December 2024 profile identifies Manuel Carrera as managing Cancún/Riviera Maya and Juan Carlos Del Rio as managing partner for Los Cabos–La Paz.
UbiComp/ISWC 2023 explicitly offered attendee transfers through a dedicated EPIC agreement.
The 2018-era brochure contains named Vistana and Tamla Travel testimonials and advertises hotel selection/contract negotiation.
uncertainties: Current Cancún event pipeline, repeat-client cadence, annual production and hotel room-night influence.
Current named hotel/resort in-house relationships, exclusivity restrictions and any existing Condesa/Posadas agreement.
Whether EPIC originates hotel demand, controls a client shortlist, contracts room blocks or only services an already-booked group on each assignment.
Current fee/commission structure and whether historical pricing claims still apply.
Current role ownership for each public contact and the exact current Cancún office mailing details.
Staffed-office coverage versus destination service coverage, and current quality certifications, insurance and operating capacity.

potential_business.title: Potential business for this hotel
potential_business.body: Strong qualitative fit, commercially unqualified. For Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive, the supplied 507-room/12-meeting-room beach-resort profile aligns with EPIC’s corporate retreats, incentives and destination meetings. EPIC could combine accommodation sourcing with airport arrivals, local activities, team-building and off-site events, complementing an all-inclusive stay. Prioritize self-contained resort programs and meeting/training groups seeking a beach setting—not assumed city-center transient business or convention-center walkability. Fit depends on actual group size, meeting configurations, dates, budget, adult/family mix and the client’s all-inclusive preference. No existing property relationship or incremental production is established.

why_act_now.title: Why act now
why_act_now.body: Request a qualification call with Manuel Carrera and Diana Esparza, using EPIC’s published company channel and asking for the current Cancún groups lead. Send a concise resort-specific sales kit: room categories, meeting layouts/capacities, all-inclusive group inclusions and exclusions, transfer logistics and sample retreat/incentive agendas. Do not offer exclusivity or forecast room nights at this stage.

facts_and_uncertainties.title: Established facts and uncertainties
facts: EPIC was established in Cancún in 1988; its official website describes more than 35 years in the industry.
The official website markets MICE, destination management, weddings, transportation, tours and golf, including hotel negotiation/arrangements.
The official destination list includes Cancún and Riviera Maya, plus other Mexican beach and cultural destinations.
A December 2024 profile identifies Manuel Carrera as managing Cancún/Riviera Maya and Juan Carlos Del Rio as managing partner for Los Cabos–La Paz.
UbiComp/ISWC 2023 explicitly offered attendee transfers through a dedicated EPIC agreement.
The 2018-era brochure contains named Vistana and Tamla Travel testimonials and advertises hotel selection/contract negotiation.
uncertainties: Current Cancún event pipeline, repeat-client cadence, annual production and hotel room-night influence.
Current named hotel/resort in-house relationships, exclusivity restrictions and any existing Condesa/Posadas agreement.
Whether EPIC originates hotel demand, controls a client shortlist, contracts room blocks or only services an already-booked group on each assignment.
Current fee/commission structure and whether historical pricing claims still apply.
Current role ownership for each public contact and the exact current Cancún office mailing details.
Staffed-office coverage versus destination service coverage, and current quality certifications, insurance and operating capacity.

Tropical’s Cancún incentive, airport-transfer, hotel-service and meeting capabilities align directly with Fiesta Americana Condesa’s Hotel Zone beachfront all-inclusive positioning and the supplied 507-room inventory. facts_and_uncertainties.title: Established facts and uncertainties
facts: The company dates its start in Cancún to 1984 and currently markets Mexico and Dominican Republic destination-management services.
Its public FAQ explicitly includes venue sourcing, contract negotiation, accommodation, transport, audiovisual production and on-site coordination.
The current official leadership page identifies Mariel Camara and Alejandro Medina in Cancún/Riviera Maya leadership roles.
Global DMC Partners has a Cancún destination listing identifying Tropical Incentives DMC.
A 2021 Posadas auction package offered Condesa as a hotel option and Tropical-provided airport transfers for two.
A March 2025 company-affiliated post describes Tropical supporting a FAM at Grand Fiesta Americana Coral Beach, not Condesa.
Condesa’s official business page advertises 12 event areas and more than 21,600 square feet/2,000 square meters of event space.
uncertainties: Current relationship status with Condesa and whether the 2021 promotional package ever converted into a stay or group booking.
Annual Cancún or Condesa room nights, group counts, room-block sizes, revenue contribution and forward pipeline.
Buyer/source-market mix and the proportion of enquiries for which Tropical influences accommodation versus ground services alone.
Actual compensation structure, contracting authority, credit exposure, cancellation terms and preferred-hotel commitments.
Which legal entity named in the multi-entity privacy notice would contract with the hotel; confirm that the published domicile is also the appropriate meeting address.
Current transfer/production capacity and insurance terms; historical presentation claims should not be treated as current contractual commitments.

Would a site inspection and one qualified pilot proposal be useful, and what measurable outcomes would justify expanding the relationship?

recommended_next_step.title: Recommended next step
recommended_next_step.body: Have the hotel’s group-sales lead request a short qualification meeting with Mariel Camara through Tropical’s official contact channel, involving Alejandro/Alex Medina for operations if appropriate. Reference the historical Posadas/Condesa package and separate Coral Beach FAM without suggesting an active Condesa agreement. Propose a property inspection and one sample resort incentive/retreat itinerary with airport transfers, meetings, a themed evening and team building. Share room categories, meeting layouts, group inclusions, AV/external-vendor rules and dates the hotel actually wants to sell. Ask Tropical to identify live, suitable enquiries and clarify who selects and contracts accommodation. Progress to a non-exclusive pilot RFP only after decision rights, economics and service responsibilities are agreed; do not promise allotments or incentives on assumed production.
qualificationQuestions: For which live Cancún enquiries do you recommend hotels before accommodation is selected, versus only operate ground services after selection?
Who holds final hotel selection, negotiates the room block and signs/pays the accommodation contract: Tropical, an agency, an association or the end client?
What historical Condesa business can you substantiate by program date, rooms picked up and repeat enquiry, subject to client confidentiality?
What are the actual origin markets, lead times, room-block needs, budget ranges and stay patterns for your current resort incentive and retreat enquiries?
Which regional meeting or training enquiries genuinely require an overnight all-inclusive resort rather than a city venue?
What conditions make Condesa competitive in your hotel shortlist, and what existing supplier arrangements or client preferences constrain selection?
Do you require commissionable rates, net rates, disclosed management fees or another arrangement; who earns each fee and how are payments and cancellations handled?
Which services would Tropical deliver versus the hotel, and how should all-inclusive meals/drinks, private functions, AV and outside-supplier access be reconciled?
Which legal entity will contract, and what insurance, contingency plans, transport standards and data/guest-manifest controls apply?
Would a site inspection and one qualified pilot proposal be useful, and what measurable outcomes would justify expanding the relationship?

uncertainties: Current annual production, share of business directed to Condesa and the value of the addressable pipeline are unverified.

Contracting authority, client approval rights, billing flow and liability allocation must be confirmed per account.

Public contact directories can lag personnel changes; confirm current assignments and title wording directly.
Undated portfolio testimonials cannot establish recent production, and the FAM evidence cannot establish converted group bookings.

potential_business.title: Potential business for this hotel
potential_business.body: Strong destination/product fit; commercially unqualified production potential. For Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive, the appropriate thesis is a residential beach-resort incentive, corporate retreat or meeting program—not city-center transient business. México Planners explicitly sells corporate retreats, incentive travel, group logistics and team-building in this destination. The supplied 507-room inventory and the hotel’s officially advertised 12 meeting rooms, more than 2,000 square meters of event space, indoor/outdoor settings and lodging-linked packages support a combined stay-and-meet proposal. Airport reception and transfers complement the airport-to-resort journey; beach activities and regional excursions complement the stay. The 2026 Grand Fiesta Americana Los Cabos FAM is a useful brand-family conversation bridge, but it is neither a Condesa Cancún relationship nor proof of a group-sales agreement. Regional training groups are a secondary hypothesis to test, not established planner demand.

why_act_now.title: Why act now
why_act_now.body: Advance to a qualification-led introduction, not a production-based preferred-partner commitment. Contact Priscilla López and request that Ana Comas or the current Cancún sales owner join. The official Cancún contact route is info.cancun@mexicoplanners.com / +52 (998) 802 1476. Reference the documented Los Cabos FAM as context without implying an existing Condesa agreement. Propose a focused property inspection covering room categories, meeting/breakout layouts, private functions, transfer staging, hospitality-desk placement, beach activities and weather alternatives. Bring a sample all-inclusive residential meeting/incentive proposal with inclusions and incremental charges separated. Before discussing commissions or concessions, confirm the decision chain and request anonymized recent Cancún program examples, room-block responsibility and suitable upcoming RFPs. Pilot one mutually qualified opportunity; avoid exclusivity or guaranteed-production assumptions.

facts_and_uncertainties.title: Established facts and uncertainties
facts: The company’s official sites identify México Planners as a full-service DMC covering Cancún, Riviera Maya, Los Cabos and Puerto Vallarta.
A dedicated Cancún office address and local contact route are publicly listed.
Corporate retreats, incentives, transportation, themed events, team-building and hospitality assistance are explicitly advertised services.
Independent July 2018 trade coverage documents joint Cancún destination promotion with hotels and meeting-planner participation.
Company and hotel-side May 2026 posts both identify collaboration on a Grand Fiesta Americana Los Cabos FAM.
The target hotel officially markets 12 meeting rooms, more than 2,000 square meters of event space, beachfront indoor/outdoor options and packages including lodging.
uncertainties: Actual Cancún production, revenue contribution, future demand, buyer mix and account concentration are unverified.
The extent of hotel-sourcing influence versus DMC-only ground handling must be established opportunity by opportunity.
No Condesa Cancún-specific relationship or booking authority is established.
Current contact remits, particularly Ana Comas’s overlapping profile roles and Los Cabos-based contacts’ Cancún coverage, require confirmation.
The exact contracting entity, financial terms, insurance, supplier compliance and cancellation/credit arrangements were not verified.
The Cancún site’s 20-year claim and IMEX’s 1997 founding statement are not interchangeable with years of Cancún-office operation.
The reviewed evidence does not provide a verified paid corporate-event case study with attendance and hotel room-night outcomes.

qualificationQuestions: For Cancún programs, do you recommend hotels, issue hotel RFPs, negotiate rates, contract room blocks, or provide only destination services after a hotel is selected?
Who is the contracting and paying party for accommodation: México Planners, an intermediary agency, or the corporate client? Who gives final property approval?
What anonymized Cancún/Riviera Maya programs have you handled in the last 12–24 months, and which involved all-inclusive beachfront hotels?
What were their actual room-block sizes, stay lengths, meeting/breakout needs, seasonality and realized room nights? Please distinguish requested, contracted and consumed production.
Which source markets and buyer segments currently drive Cancún demand? Does the Costa Rican FAM activity translate into Cancún opportunities, or only Los Cabos?
Are corporate retreats and incentives the main fit, or do you also have residential training/meeting requirements suited to this resort?
Which live opportunities could consider Condesa Cancún, and what budget, dates, cancellation terms and client decision deadlines apply?
What commercial structure is required—commissionable rate, net rate, referral arrangement or separate DMC fee—and what legal entity would sign?
What existing supplier preferences or restrictions affect hotel selection? Is any exclusivity requested or already binding?
How should airport transfers, hospitality desks, external production, gifts, beach activities and off-property dining be coordinated with hotel policies and all-inclusive inclusions?
Would a property inspection or joint FAM be useful, who should attend, and what measurable follow-up would justify hosted support?

qualificationQuestions: For Cancún programs, do you recommend hotels, issue hotel RFPs, negotiate rates, contract room blocks, or provide only destination services after a hotel is selected?
Who is the contracting and paying party for accommodation: México Planners, an intermediary agency, or the corporate client? Who gives final property approval?
What anonymized Cancún/Riviera Maya programs have you handled in the last 12–24 months, and which involved all-inclusive beachfront hotels?
What were their actual room-block sizes, stay lengths, meeting/breakout needs, seasonality and realized room nights? Please distinguish requested, contracted and consumed production.
Which source markets and buyer segments currently drive Cancún demand? Does the Costa Rican FAM activity translate into Cancún opportunities, or only Los Cabos?
Are corporate retreats and incentives the main fit, or do you also have residential training/meeting requirements suited to this resort?
Which live opportunities could consider Condesa Cancún, and what budget, dates, cancellation terms and client decision deadlines apply?
What commercial structure is required—commissionable rate, net rate, referral arrangement or separate DMC fee—and what legal entity would sign?
What existing supplier preferences or restrictions affect hotel selection? Is any exclusivity requested or already binding?
How should airport transfers, hospitality desks, external production, gifts, beach activities and off-property dining be coordinated with hotel policies and all-inclusive inclusions?
Would a property inspection or joint FAM be useful, who should attend, and what measurable follow-up would justify hosted support?

facts_and_uncertainties.title: Established facts and uncertainties
facts: The official site identifies DMC Cancun as a meeting-planning, event-production and destination-management company and claims more than 10 years of relevant experience.
The official service list explicitly includes site inspections, facility negotiations, hotel contract review and room-block/cut-off/attrition management.
The official geographic scope extends from Cancún to Tulum; the company profile also names Costa Mujeres.
The company profile reports a 2011 founding date; Gabriela Macedo and Fernando Llano each list DMC Cancún leadership roles beginning January 2011.
Gabriela Macedo is publicly listed as Owner/Director of Sales and Fernando Llano as President & CEO.
A company-authored February 2020 post documents a self-reported dine-around logistics example; a separate DMC-CANCUN 2026 excursion page displays Actalent branding.
The hotel’s official meetings materials report 507 rooms, over 21,600 square feet of indoor meeting space, outdoor event options and a private group check-in foyer.
uncertainties: Legal contracting identity and current physical office address.
Current independently verified client roster, event dates, volumes, hotel room-night production and future pipeline.
Whether historical testimonials represent DMC Cancún engagements or the principals’ prior employment.
Whether the reported nine-year recurring VIP program remains active, who the client is, and which hotels it uses.
Exact relationship to the Actalent-branded 2026 excursion site and any authority to select accommodation for that program.
Hotel signing authority, client mandates, commission/fee structure, exclusivity and existing supplier agreements.
Current operating resources and technology, insurance, transport compliance and financial capacity.
Actual fit of client budgets, rooming patterns, meeting layouts and service expectations with this specific all-inclusive resort.

qualificationQuestions: For the next 12 months, which Cancún group briefs can you discuss by dates, room-block size, nights, meeting format, budget and decision stage?
For each opportunity, do you recommend hotels, run the RFP, negotiate rates, manage pickup or sign the agreement? Who makes the final selection and pays the hotel?
What proportion of recent placements used all-inclusive beach resorts, and what made those programs commercially and operationally successful?
Which client origin markets and group types are active today? Do you have corporate retreats, incentives, regional training or association meetings suitable for this property?
Can you share recent references and anonymized contracted-versus-actual room pickup, cancellations and attrition outcomes?
Have you placed business at this property or other Fiesta Americana/Posadas hotels? Are any existing commercial agreements or conflicts relevant?
How are you compensated—client fee, supplier markup, commission or another arrangement—and how is that disclosed? Are rates gross or net and who handles taxes and payment risk?
Who operates the 2026 Actalent-branded excursion program, what is your exact role, and may the client be contacted as a reference?
Which services would remain in-house at the resort versus with your team, and how would private dining, production and off-property activities be priced against all-inclusive inclusions?
Please confirm the legal entity, current office, operating team, insurance, transport-provider compliance, emergency procedures and ability to execute concurrent groups.

recommended_next_step.title: Recommended next step
recommended_next_step.body: Advance to a non-exclusive qualification call with Gabriela Macedo, involving Fernando Llano for partnership terms. Use the official public inquiry address info@dmc-cancun.com and ask for routing to them. Lead with the resort’s integrated all-inclusive meeting proposition, not a commission promise. Request a recent anonymized hotel-sourcing example and a forward group brief, then offer a focused site inspection covering guestrooms, meeting layouts, private check-in, banquet options, outdoor weather backup, transfer staging and outside-vendor requirements. Pilot one suitable RFP before discussing preferred status or production targets.
qualificationQuestions: For the next 12 months, which Cancún group briefs can you discuss by dates, room-block size, nights, meeting format, budget and decision stage?
For each opportunity, do you recommend hotels, run the RFP, negotiate rates, manage pickup or sign the agreement? Who makes the final selection and pays the hotel?
What proportion of recent placements used all-inclusive beach resorts, and what made those programs commercially and operationally successful?
Which client origin markets and group types are active today? Do you have corporate retreats, incentives, regional training or association meetings suitable for this property?
Can you share recent references and anonymized contracted-versus-actual room pickup, cancellations and attrition outcomes?
Have you placed business at this property or other Fiesta Americana/Posadas hotels? Are any existing commercial agreements or conflicts relevant?
How are you compensated—client fee, supplier markup, commission or another arrangement—and how is that disclosed? Are rates gross or net and who handles taxes and payment risk?
Who operates the 2026 Actalent-branded excursion program, what is your exact role, and may the client be contacted as a reference?
Which services would remain in-house at the resort versus with your team, and how would private dining, production and off-property activities be priced against all-inclusive inclusions?
Please confirm the legal entity, current office, operating team, insurance, transport-provider compliance, emergency procedures and ability to execute concurrent groups.
